messages.author: b9ac49083245e671
messages.subject: Academic Performance
parts:
Hi. I'm a student and need help with a project of SEM. I want to predict the academic performance in Mathematics. I have a set of questions that measures concepts like Math self-concept, Motivation, etc and the scores of Math Test.  I've read some articles but I haven't found how to link the observed variable 'Math Calification' to my model. For this moment I have this:



f1 =~ C9 + C8 + C6 + C10 + C3 + C11 + C1 + C14
f2 =~ RA17 + A13 + RA22 + A8 + A18
f3 =~ A21 + A6 + RA16 + A24
f4 =~ C40 + C39
f5 =~ C32 + C33 + C35

exa.alg ~ f2 + f3

Where the C's, RA's, A's are the answers to the questions about motivation, math self-concept, etc. and 'exa.alg' are the califications of the Math Test.

So, basically, THIS IS MY QUESTION:

Does a regression on f2 and f3, where f2 and f3 are latent variables, predict the academic performance correctly?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Academic Performance
parts: Does a regression on f2 and f3, where f2 and f3 are latent variables, predict the academic performance correctly?

In any case, the answer to your question would not be Yes/No, it would be a matter of degree.  You can look at the rsquare for an idea of the (asymptotically expected) correspondence between observed and predicted values.

Terry
